blocks.text: Har component ka apna khaas retardation factor (rukawat ka number) hota hai jise Rf value kehte hain. Rf value yun nikalti hai:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein ek jagah 'Rr value' chhapa hai; sahi 'Rf value' hai.

blocks.latex: R_f = \frac{\text{Distance travelled by a component from the original spot}}{\text{Distance travelled by solvent from the original spot}}
blocks.text_alt: Rf = Distance travelled by a component from the original spot / Distance travelled by solvent from the original spot

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Dono faasle (distances) ek hi jagah se naape jate hain: asal spot wali pencil lakeer (base line) se. Component kabhi solvent se aage nahi jata, is liye Rf hamesha 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hota hai aur is ki koi unit nahi hoti.
Figure 15.10 ka chromatogram dikhata hai ke sample A mein B aur C dono components hain. B aur C ki Rf values yeh hain:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki tasveer mein faaslon par sirf '1' chhapa hai (ek faasla to do spots ke beech naapa gaya hai), aur text mein Rf(B) aur Rf(C) dono ko x/y likha hai. Sahi yeh hai: har faasla base line se naapa jata hai; B (neela spot) ka faasla x aur C (kaala spot) ka faasla x' hai, is liye Rf(B) = x/y aur Rf(C) = x'/y.

blocks.alt: Teen namoonon A, B aur C ka chromatogram. A mein ek kaala (oopar) aur ek neela (neeche) spot; B mein sirf neela, C mein sirf kaala. y base line se solvent front tak faasla; x aur x' base line se neele aur kaale spot tak faasle.
blocks.caption: Figure 15.10: Chromatogram (kitab ki Figure 15.10 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: A ke dono spots B aur C ke spots ki seedh mein hain, is liye A impure hai aur us mein B aur C dono hain. y base line se solvent front tak ka faasla hai; x neele spot tak aur x' kaale spot tak.

Paper chromatography se aasani se pata chalta hai ke chemical reaction mein bana madda pure (khalis) hai ya impure, bas aisa solvent lena hota hai jis mein madda hal ho jaye. Pure madda chromatogram par ek spot deta hai, jabke impure madda ek se zyada spots deta hai.
Paper chromatogram se maddon ko pehchana bhi ja sakta hai: unhen pure maddon ke maloom samples se mila kar dekha jata hai. Jin do maddon ki Rf values barabar hon, woh ghaliban ek hi madda hain.

blocks.title: Dilchasp maloomat
blocks.text: Paper chromatography mein istemal hone wala Whatman filter paper khaas chune hue cotton cellulose se banta hai. Whatman filter paper No. 1 aam kaam ke liye hai; is ki retention (zarraat rokne ki salahiyat) aur flow rate (behne ki raftar) darmiyani hai. Is ke pores ka size 11 μm hai.

Figure 15.10 ke chromatogram mein impure madde mein do components hain, kyun ke us ne do rangeen spots diye hain. Impure madde ke spots utna hi faasla chale hain jitna reference ke pure compounds. Agar stationary phase aur mobile phase wahi rahen to kisi madde ki Rf value hamesha ek jaisi rehti hai.

blocks.caption: Chromatogram parhna
rows: known pure sample jaisi Rf par spot

blocks.prompt: Ek component base line se 3.0 cm chala aur solvent front 6.0 cm. Rf value kya hai?
blocks.explanation: Rf = component ka faasla ÷ solvent ka faasla = 3.0 cm ÷ 6.0 cm = 0.5. Dono faasle base line se naape jate hain; units cancel ho jati hain.

blocks.prompt: Rf value aur us ka istemal bayan karein. Agar do components stationary phase se taqreeban barabar chipakte hon to kya hoga?
blocks.explanation: Rf = component ka faasla ÷ solvent front ka faasla, dono base line se. Wahi phases hon to kisi madde ki Rf hamesha ek rehti hai, is liye is se madda pehchana jata hai aur purity jaanchi jati hai (pure madda = ek spot). Agar do components barabar chipakte hon to woh taqreeban ek raftar se chalte hain aur un ke spots ek doosre par aa jate hain; unhen alag karne ke liye solvent badalna parta hai.

items: Rf = component ka faasla ÷ solvent front ka faasla (dono base line se); Rf 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan, koi unit nahi.
Wahi phases mein madde ki Rf hamesha wahi; ek spot = pure, zyada spots = impure; known sample se Rf mila kar madda pehchana jata hai.
